author: Khan Academy
description:
Gauss’s law relates electric flux through a Gaussian surface to the charge enclosed by that surface. A Gaussian surface is a three-dimensional, closed surface. The total electric flux through a Gaussian surface is independent of the size of the Gaussian surface if the amount of enclosed charge remains constant. Gaussian surfaces are typically constructed such that the electric field generated by the enclosed charge is either perpendicular or parallel to different regions of the Gaussian surface, resulting in a simplified surface integral. 

Sections:
00:00 - Flux through a cube
06:51 - Electric field outside a uniformly charged sphere
11:31 - Electric field inside a uniformly charged sphere
